# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Parent: seed (baseline). Val at parent: reward 0.230 — 0 solid / 8 flaky / 2 failing of 10 tasks. This is the first real iteration; no prior_iterations to build on (RUNMAP/LEDGER empty).

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag (KNOWLEDGE / BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP) | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Booking payment/amount errors | book flows (e.g. task 8 single-certificate) | agent leaves payment `amount` blank or mis-keys the payment dict (`id`/bare string), causing opaque pydantic/"does not add up" failures | BEHAVIORAL | in-body normalization + deterministic single-payment amount fill + enriched errors |
| 2 | Wrong baggage count | task 12 (gold econ) + all baggage books | agent passes a wrong `nonfree_baggages`; the paid-bag count is fully determined by membership×cabin×#passengers | KNOWLEDGE→CODE | in-body recompute of `nonfree_baggages` from the policy allowance table |
| 3 | Cancelling ineligible reservations | task 37 (IFOYYZ: basic economy, no insurance, >24h) | agent cancels a reservation that meets none of the four cancellation conditions (or one whose flights have flown) | BEHAVIORAL | 2-layer in-body eligibility guard (flown → refuse; no-condition → refuse) |
| 4 | Passenger-name correction | update_passengers flows | agent blanks/changes a date of birth or the passenger count when only a name should change | BEHAVIORAL | dob key normalization + count-mismatch enriched error + policy line |
| 5 | Wrong-reservation reasoning | tasks 17 / 22 | agent acts on / cancel-rebuilds a different reservation than the one asked about | BEHAVIORAL | prose guardrail only (too entangled with dialogue to guard in code safely) |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes, incl. a NEW tool when a cluster needs one)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | in-body normalization + computation | tools.py `book_reservation` | `_normalize_payment_dict` (bare str/`id`→`payment_id`, drop `type`/`source`, coerce `amount`→int) + `_normalize_passenger_dict` (any dob alias→`dob`); when exactly ONE payment method, set its amount to the exact computed total. Enriched "not found"/balance/"does not add up" errors list the user's real payment ids + balances. | Yes — a correct single amount already equals the total, so the override is identity; normalization only fixes malformed shapes; multi-method splits are still validated, not auto-filled. |
| 2 | in-body computation | tools.py `book_reservation`, `update_reservation_baggages` | recompute `nonfree_baggages = max(0, total_baggages − free_allowance×#passengers)` from `_FREE_BAGGAGE_ALLOWANCE`. | Yes — an already-correct count maps to itself (verified: all val gold baggage counts recompute to their existing value / 0). |
| 3 | in-body guard | tools.py `cancel_reservation` | (1) any flight status in {flying,landed} → refuse (transfer); (2) if NOT within-24h AND not business AND no insurance AND no airline-cancelled segment → refuse. | Yes — fires only when policy forbids cancelling; verified it never blocks the gold-cancel reservations (Z7GOZK, K1NW8N). |
| 4 | normalization + enriched error + prose | tools.py `update_reservation_passengers`; policy.md "Change passengers" | dob-alias normalization; error states current vs provided count; policy line: send ALL passengers, reuse existing dob, never change an unrequested dob. | Yes — normalization only rewrites keys; the count check restates an existing hard rule; prose is additive. |
| 4b | enriched error | tools.py `update_reservation_flights` | payment-not-found now lists the user's real payment ids before `_payment_for_update`. | Yes — only changes the message on an already-failing path. |
| 5 | prose only | policy.md "Cancel flight" | "basic economy is not a barrier to cancellation"; "if no condition holds, do not cancel or cancel-and-rebuild"; "act only on the exact reservation the user asks about". | Additive clarifications consistent with existing policy; no new permission granted. |
| 1 | prose only | policy.md "Book flight" Payment | documents the `{payment_id, amount}` shape and that a single method pays the full total. | Additive; mirrors the code behavior for the mid-tier reader. |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/computation/new-tool now does on those exact inputs)
- book_reservation (cluster 1/2): real-DB book with `payment_methods=[{'payment_id': gift_card, ...}]`, no amount, insurance=yes, total_baggages=1 → amount auto-filled to 130 (=100 flight + 30 insurance), nonfree recomputed to 0 (gold econ), gift card balance 300→170. Malformed `{'id': cert}` also normalized; single-cert-over-balance case raises the enriched balance error (bal 100 < 122).
- update_reservation_baggages (cluster 2): `YAX4DR` (gold, economy, 2 pax) called with wrong `nonfree_baggages=2` → recomputed to 0 (matches gold task 12).
- cancel_reservation (cluster 3): Z7GOZK (insurance=yes) → ALLOWED; K1NW8N (created within 24h) → ALLOWED; NQNU5R (flights landed) → BLOCKED-flown; IFOYYZ (basic econ, no ins, >24h) → BLOCKED-no-condition (this is the task-37 wrong cancel).
- update_reservation_passengers (cluster 4): dict passengers with `date_of_birth` alias normalize to `dob`; a wrong count raises an error naming current vs provided count.
- Syntax + import: `ast.parse` OK; module imports cleanly under the tau2 venv.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used (or: "serial fallback because …"): Serial — single small edit space (two files), all verification done directly against the real airline DB via the tau2 venv python; parallel fan-out would not add signal for a 2-file edit.
- Prior iterations I read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md (which, and what I learned): none exist yet (seed baseline only; RUNMAP/LEDGER/JOURNAL empty). Established the first baseline of clusters + verified guards for successors to build on.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- Single-payment amount auto-fill + payment/passenger dict normalization in book_reservation (proven identity on correct inputs).
- nonfree_baggages recompute from the allowance table (both book + update_baggages).
- The 2-layer cancel eligibility guard — verified it never blocks a legitimate (gold) cancel.
- Enriched actionable errors listing real payment ids/balances instead of opaque pydantic errors.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- Multi-payment split auto-allocation: NOT auto-filled (regression risk — cannot know the intended split); handled with an enriched error instead.
- Cluster 5 (wrong-reservation reasoning, tasks 17/22): no safe code guard exists (entangled with the dialogue), so only an additive prose guardrail was added; left as the main un-cracked cluster for a successor.
- Cabin-change refund/price logic: currently passing in the traces I inspected; not touched to avoid blast radius.
